data.one_liner: A simple library to read, write, and manipulate Java-style properties files in Dart.
data.what_it_does: The properties package enables parsing and managing key-value configuration files. It supports typed getters for primitives and lists, default fallbacks, and event streams for property modifications. It also provides methods to filter entries, export to JSON, and save changes back to files.
use_when: Reading or writing Java-style .properties configuration files in Dart applications.
Accessing configuration key-values with automatic parsing to types like int, double, bool, or List.
Listening to changes when properties are added or updated in a configuration store.
avoid_when: Managing structured or hierarchical configuration formats such as JSON, YAML, or TOML.
Web-only Flutter apps where direct file-based properties operations are not applicable.
strengths: Provides typed accessor methods (getInt, getDouble, getBool, getList) with fallback support.
Includes event streams (e.g., onAdd) to react to property changes.
Supports JSON serialization and filtering via custom predicates.
weaknesses: Outdated README notes stating file output is unsupported, contradicting changelog additions like saveToFile.
Limited formatting and comment-preservation capabilities compared to modern config parsers.

alternatives.name: cli_config
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick cli_config when dealing with standard Dart CLI configurations and environment variable overrides.
